questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Para and ortho hydrogen differ in:
questions.solution:
Hydrogen gas exists in two isomeric forms known as ortho-hydrogen and para-hydrogen.

In ortho-hydrogen, the spins of the two nuclei (protons) are in the same direction (parallel).

In para-hydrogen, the spins of the two nuclei (protons) are in opposite directions (antiparallel).

Both forms have the same atomic number, the same number of neutrons (zero in the case of protium), and the same size, as they are both molecules of $H_2$.

Therefore, they differ only in the relative orientation of the nuclear spins.

Answer: Spins of protons

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Decomposition of hydrogen peroxide can be prevented by adding
questions.solution:
The decomposition of hydrogen peroxide ($H_2O_2$) is a catalytic reaction that is often accelerated by impurities, dust, or metal surfaces. To stabilize $H_2O_2$ and prevent its decomposition, negative catalysts or stabilizers are added to the solution.

Acetanilide, phosphoric acid, and urea are commonly used as stabilizers for hydrogen peroxide. These substances act by inhibiting the catalytic activity of trace metal ions that would otherwise promote the decomposition of $H_2O_2$ into water and oxygen.

Among the given options, urea acts as a stabilizer for hydrogen peroxide.

Answer: urea

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect for $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$ structure?
options: It has an open book structure.
It $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ bond length is 145.8 and $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ is 98.8 .
questions.solution:
The structure of hydrogen peroxide ($\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2$) is non-planar and is commonly described as an open book structure.

In the gaseous phase, the dihedral angle between the two O-H planes is approximately $111.5^{\circ}$, not $180^{\circ}$. A dihedral angle of $180^{\circ}$ would imply a planar structure, which is not the case for $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2$.

The $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ bond length in $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2$ is $145.8$ pm and the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond length is $98.8$ pm.

The dihedral angle (angle between the two planes containing the O-H bonds) in the solid state is $90.2^{\circ}$.

Since the dihedral angle is not $180^{\circ}$, the statement that its dihedral angle is $180^{\circ}$ is incorrect.

Answer: Its dihedral angle is $180^{\circ}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the hydrides of group 15 in correct decreasing order of reducing nature.
questions.solution:
The reducing nature of the hydrides of group 15 elements depends on the stability of the M-H bond. As we move down the group from N to Bi, the atomic size of the central atom increases, which leads to a decrease in the bond dissociation enthalpy of the M-H bond.

The bond strength decreases in the order $\mathrm{NH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{PH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{AsH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{SbH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{BiH}_{3}$.

Since the reducing character is directly proportional to the ease of releasing hydrogen atoms, the reducing nature increases as the bond strength decreases. Therefore, the correct decreasing order of reducing nature is $\mathrm{BiH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{SbH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{AsH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{PH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{NH}_{3}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{BiH}_{3}\gt \mathrm{SbH}_{3}\gt \mathrm{AsH}_{3}\gt \mathrm{PH}_{3}\gt \mathrm{NH}_{3}$
